description.narrative: Bangladesh continues to face food insecurity and nutrition challenges, alongside a large base of consumers with limited purchasing power. The Project is expected to strengthen market access for smallholder dairy farmers by expanding the companys supplier network, supported by supply chain development, farmer training, feed support, and improved access to credit. It is also expected to increase the availability of safe, nutritious dairy products and lower sugar beverages for consumers. More broadly, the Project is anticipated to contribute to job creation, stronger formal employment, higher agricultural productivity, and wider economic linkages in Bangladesh. Besides, the beverage market is currently characterized by very high sugar consumption, with the vast majority of carbonated and dairy beverages containing high sugar levels, posing material health concerns. The Project aims to introduce and scale lower-sugar beverages through PRAN, a market leader, setting a visible benchmark that could catalyze broader industry reformulation over time.

The group of companies known as PRAN Group (PRAN or the Group) was established in 1981. The Group is a leading branded food and beverage group and the largest Agro processer in Bangladesh. PRAN is a well-known household brand in Bangladesh and produces more than four hundred food products across multiple categories including juices, drinks and beverages, dairy, confectionary, snacks, grains, spices, and frozen foods. PRAN exports to 145 countries across the world. IFC will provide long-term US Dollar financing to be utilized to support expansion plans across the two group companies, Pran Dairy Limited (PDL) and Mymensingh Agro Limited (MAL).
